Show key name, a nonsecret identifier or suffix, creation date and status in the table. Show the full secret only during creation, with explicit copy and storage guidance; subsequent visits should not retrieve it. If reveal is an established requirement, make it deliberate, time limited and keyboard accessible. Never include secrets in announcements or error logs.

Give each Copy button an accessible name such as ‘Copy API key for Production’; report clipboard success or failure through a polite status region and persistent inline feedback. Keep Rename as a routine action. Place Revoke in a clearly separated destructive menu or area. Its confirmation names the key, explains that dependent integrations will stop, and offers Cancel as the safe initial focus. Disable duplicate submissions while awaiting the response. Do not promise undo for irreversible revocation; explain replacement and rotation recovery.

Keep forms and entered values mounted after errors. Associate field errors with inputs, announce a concise summary and focus the first invalid field or summary. On cancellation restore focus to the trigger; after revocation focus the next logical row or heading. Retain success feedback until dismissed or until the next relevant action. On narrow screens reflow each row into labeled fields, with readable labels, visible focus and adequate touch targets.
answers.verification: Proposed checks: complete creation, copy, rename and cancellation using keyboard and a screen reader; test clipboard/network failures, zoom, narrow layouts and focus after row removal. This is a specification; no interface was implemented or tested.

Use version-specific pagination. For v3, continue with each returned cursor and stop only when next_cursor is null [Q1]. A short page is not the stated completion signal, so the current integration can omit later records. That omission is an inference from the contract, not an observed production result. Q2 establishes that v2 uses page numbers; it does not establish v2’s termination rule. Q3’s third-party empty-page loop is weaker evidence and cannot override the v3 contract.

Propose an entirely local fixture experiment comparing the existing short-page loop, Q3’s empty-count loop and a cursor-aware loop. Include a short nonterminal page, an empty page with a nonnull cursor, and a full terminal page with next_cursor=null. Assert the exact collected records, cursor sequence and termination count. Add repeated-cursor and malformed-response fixtures so the client fails visibly within a page/deadline budget instead of looping or reporting partial data as complete.

Decision: adopt cursor termination for v3 [Q1], retain an explicit v2 adapter only after its completion contract is supplied [Q2], and do not transplant Q3 across versions. Release criteria would be complete fixture traversal, bounded failure behavior and an explicit API-version configuration. No requests or experiments have been performed; real cursor-expiry, ordering and retry guarantees remain unspecified.
answers.verification: Proposed checks only: run the local contract fixtures and compare exact request arguments and collected IDs against fixture expectations. No network requests, sources beyond Q1–Q3, or measured results are claimed.

Provide preview as the default and an explicit apply mode with the same structured plan. Accept repository, destination, base revision and branch as separate arguments; launch Git with argument arrays, never shell interpolation. Resolve the repository root and destination against a documented root, normalize '..', and check existing ancestors for symlinks or Windows junctions before enforcing containment. Show resolved paths, base commit, branch action and expected writes.

Preflight repository ownership/trust, Git availability, base validity, source dirty state, worktree registrations, destination existence and branch use. Preserve source edits. Refuse an existing destination, an existing branch or a branch checked out elsewhere unless the user explicitly selects a supported reuse operation; never force checkout, reset, delete or move user content. Recheck under a per-repository lock because preview can become stale.

Journal a unique operation ID and completed phases before mutations, recording only resources created by this operation. After interruption inspect both journal and actual Git metadata. Resume idempotently when ownership and expected state match; otherwise return a conflict with precise recovery instructions. Cleanup must stop if new edits appear and must never remove unrelated files or branches.

Document stable exits: 0 success/preview, 2 invalid input, 3 collision, 4 environment/Git failure, 5 incomplete recoverable operation, 130 interruption. Keep machine-readable results on stdout and diagnostics on stderr.
answers.verification: Proposed isolated-fixture checks: spaces/Unicode, traversal and junctions, dirty destinations, existing branches, concurrent invocations, and interruption at each journal phase. No Git commands or filesystem moves were performed.

Lease expiry ends A’s authority even if A has not noticed it. Renewal checks in A are useful for stopping work but cannot prevent a paused process from later issuing an old write. Assign every successful acquisition a durable, strictly increasing fencing generation from the coordination authority. Suppose A receives 41 and B receives 42.

The storage system must atomically validate the generation at the same commit boundary as the state update. Once generation 42 is installed or B’s write commits with 42, a write carrying 41 must fail without modifying state. A read-then-check in the worker is insufficient. Use a transactional owner-generation condition, or storage-maintained maximum fencing token plus an update/version condition. For the same generation, also protect against reordered writes with an expected state version or operation sequence.

On rejection, A stops using that claim, discards stale computed state and reacquires before reading fresh state and recomputing. Retry transient errors with bounded jitter and deadlines; reuse durable operation identity after ambiguous timeouts and inspect recorded results rather than blindly replaying.

Proposed failure test: pause A after reading state, expire its lease, let B acquire 42 and commit, then resume A’s 41 write. Assert storage rejection and preservation of B’s state. A lease alone cannot guarantee exactly-once external effects; those require downstream idempotency or reconciliation.
answers.verification: Proposed checks: deterministic stale-owner interleaving, delayed/reordered writes, failed renewal, lost commit reply and coordinator restart. Confirm atomic conditional-write semantics in the actual storage; no simulation or cluster test was executed.

To submit a task, call POST /tasks with Authorization and a request_id. Keep the request_id for retries: submitting it again returns the original task. Treat it as the identity of one submission and use a new value for a genuinely new task.

Illustrative, unexecuted request notation:

POST /tasks
Authorization: <your authorization value>
request_id: <stable identifier for this submission>

The packet does not specify whether request_id belongs in a header or body, the authorization scheme, or the task payload schema. The notation above identifies required information rather than claiming a copyable wire format. Confirm those details before writing an executable client.

HTTP 202 means the task was accepted; it does not mean the task completed. Obtain the task identifier from the accepted task representation, then use GET /tasks/{id}, substituting that identifier. The task state is pending, completed or failed. Pending requires later observation; completed is the successful terminal state; failed is a terminal failure requiring investigation. Response field names are unspecified.

If authorization or required information is rejected, correct it before resubmitting. If a submission times out, retry using the same request_id to recover the original task rather than creating another. Do not interpret a polling network error as task failure. Use bounded polling/backoff; no polling interval or error-code mapping is specified.
answers.verification: Proposed checks: validate the eventual wire example against the request/response schema, verify duplicate request_id behavior and 202-to-terminal-state handling. The supplied contract lacks field placement and exact response schemas; no requests were executed.

Use a bounded single-producer/single-consumer protocol only if this ISR is truly the sole producer and one task is the sole consumer. The ISR owns the write index; the task owns the read index. Publish a sample only after its payload is complete, and consume only published entries. Use target-supported atomics and memory ordering, or a short ISR-safe critical section appropriate to Zephyr’s interrupt/SMP configuration; volatile alone provides no synchronization. A task mutex cannot protect an ISR.

Detect full before writing. A straightforward policy is drop-newest, increment a safe overrun counter and expose a data-gap indication to the consumer. Never silently overwrite unread samples. Drop-oldest would require a different synchronized ownership protocol because the producer would modify consumer state. Keep ISR work preallocated, bounded and nonblocking, and size the ring from arrival rate and maximum service delay.

For the 16-bit tick, compute elapsed with unsigned modular subtraction: elapsed = (uint16_t)(now - start), then compare with the timeout duration. State tick units and require observation before a full 65,536-tick wrap elapses; multiple wraps cannot be inferred. Signed deadline-ordering techniques require intervals below half the range. Use a wider monotonic source for longer gaps.

Proposed host tests cover full/empty transitions and rollover. Actual board validation must measure atomic tick reads, interrupt latency, sustained overruns, RAM/stack use and peripheral timing.
answers.verification: Proposed checks: interleave producer/consumer publication, fill to capacity, verify drop counters, and compare start=65530 with now=4. Target timing, SMP barriers, interrupt masking and clock behavior remain unvalidated on hardware.

Move simulation to _physics_process and express movement in units per second. First identify the existing reference render rate and record distance, acceleration, jump height and airtime so the conversion preserves the intended feel. A displacement of d pixels each frame at reference rate f corresponds to speed d × f. Preserve the existing acceleration and directional rules; normalize diagonal movement only if the intended controls require equal directional speed.

For a CharacterBody2D, set velocity in pixels per second and call move_and_slide(), which integrates velocity itself. Apply delta to acceleration/gravity changes, not again to the velocity passed through that API. If directly changing position, displacement needs delta instead.

Treat jump as a press edge rather than a continuously held action. Consume each queued press once in physics, subject to the existing grounded/jump rules. Preserve deliberate buffering, coyote time or variable jump height if present; do not introduce them as incidental fixes.

Pause the gameplay simulation through the scene lifecycle, clear accumulated elapsed time and stale queued actions on resume, and rebase any wall-clock timers. Bound exceptional steps or catch-up work so suspension time cannot become one huge movement.

Proposed tests compare equal-duration travel, collision outcomes, jump counts and trajectories at varied render rates and under stalls. Include holding jump, rapid presses, pause while moving and resuming after minutes.
answers.verification: Proposed Godot tests: compare 30/60/144 render FPS with fixed physics settings against recorded feel tolerances, inspect edge consumption and resume behavior, then play on target hardware. No engine execution or gameplay measurement was performed.

The reported 99% accuracy matches an always-negative predictor at 1% prevalence, so it establishes no useful detection performance. The maintenance field leaks the target because it exists only after failure; remove it and audit every feature’s availability at the prediction timestamp. Define the failure horizon, minimum warning time and what intervention a positive prediction triggers.

Build point-in-time windows and labels before evaluation. Deployment requires generalization to both unseen machines and a later quarter: reserve a final future-time cohort of entirely held-out machines, with no records from those machines in training. Use earlier group-disjoint, forward-time folds for tuning. Purge windows whose feature or outcome intervals cross split cutoffs, and prevent overlapping windows or duplicate events from straddling partitions. If suitable future unseen-machine data is unavailable, state that limitation explicitly.

Put imputation, scaling, feature selection and any resampling inside a scikit-learn Pipeline fitted only within training folds. Compare a dummy classifier and a simple interpretable baseline using identical splits.

Report positive events, machines and windows; precision-recall AUC, recall at an acceptable alert budget, precision, calibration and warning-time distribution. Select thresholds on validation, then evaluate the sealed test once. Estimate uncertainty by machine/event rather than treating correlated windows as independent. Inspect machine type and quarter slices; require useful event detection and acceptable false alerts before claiming deployment relevance.
answers.verification: Proposed checks: feature availability audit, machine-ID disjointness, interval-overlap purge, train-only transforms, baseline comparison and machine-clustered uncertainty. No training or evaluation was performed; the 99% figure is supplied evidence only.

Do not promote on the slightly higher offline score alone. Input drift indicates a changed operating population or pipeline, not measured accuracy loss. First distinguish genuine population change from schema, missingness, units and preprocessing defects. Retain the incumbent while investigating unless predefined safety or service thresholds require a fallback.

Evaluate both models on the same accepted, leakage-safe labeled cohort with uncertainty and important slices. Bundle each model immutably with its exact preprocessor, feature schema/order/types, dependencies, code/data identities and evaluation. Different preprocessing versions make swapping weights alone unsafe. Require clean-load and offline/serving prediction parity, plus wrong-order, missing-field and invalid-type checks.

The doubled p95 latency must be measured under representative concurrency and hardware against the service latency budget, including preprocessing and cold starts. If it violates that budget, reject promotion despite the quality increment; otherwise assess whether the quality gain justifies the cost.

Monitor input and prediction drift, schema errors, missingness, latency, failures and resource use against seasonal reference windows with sustained-alert thresholds and a named owner. Join labels after three weeks by prediction ID and version; assess mature cohorts only, tracking label coverage, quality and calibration separately.

Propose shadow evaluation followed by a bounded canary only after gates pass. Keep an immutable compatible incumbent bundle ready; rollback on predefined quality/service breaches, then reconcile affected predictions. Actual promotion remains unperformed.
answers.verification: Proposed checks: artifact round-trip, schema rejection, serving parity, representative load, delayed-label joins, synthetic drift and rollback rehearsal. No deployment, latency benchmark, accuracy measurement or traffic change was executed.

Make durable local state the source for editable drafts and pending mutations; component memory is only a view. Persist each accepted edit transactionally rather than relying on a background callback, since the OS can kill the process without one. Version the stored schema, restore before rendering editable data, and distinguish saved locally, syncing, failed and synchronized states.

Create a stable client item ID and durable operation ID before enqueueing a create. Atomically save the optimistic item and outbox entry. Retry the same operation ID and payload with bounded backoff; the server must durably deduplicate and return the original result. A client-only queue cannot guarantee this. Persist acknowledgment before removing the outbox entry, preserving the client row key when a server ID arrives. Define conflicts using server versions and explicit reconciliation, rather than silently overwriting drafts.

Own AppState/connectivity subscriptions in the appropriate lifecycle scope and remove them on unmount. Cancel or ignore stale async responses using a generation/version check. Resume synchronization after restoration and connectivity recovery without starting duplicate drainers.

Use stable keys in a virtualized FlatList. Profile representative long lists before changing rendering: measure row render counts, JS frame time, scrolling and input responsiveness. Move expensive derived work out of render, memoize only demonstrated hotspots and keep row props stable. Proposed device tests cover offline edits, background/kill/relaunch, lost server replies, duplicate retries and conflict recovery.
answers.verification: Proposed checks: real Android/iOS process restoration, offline outbox replay, server-committed/lost-reply deduplication, schema migration and conflicts. Profile release builds on representative low-end devices; no device or simulator measurements were performed.
